doc.title: Jim Cullum interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 12, 2007

title: Dancing at the club and jazz as dance music
summary: The club has small tables and no dance floor, but Cullum says the music is great dance music and was originally for dancing.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: Well I sure hope to get down there someday but I was wondering, do you have a dancing crowd? © Hamilton College Jazz Archive -4-
It’s a very small place. It’s little tables and they’re all jammed in and people are real crowded and there’s not a dance floor.
Okay. Would you prefer there was one? Do you play ever for people to dance or not?

We do play dances once in a while and the music is great dance music, as you know. It’s the ultimate dance music. It’s fun to dance to it. Sometimes people have an idea that because it’s — so many decades have passed since it was dance music that they’re not supposed to be dancing to it. But it’s great dance music and we do play for dancing. That was originally what the music was, it was music for people to dance to.
